title: Morpho-kinematics of the wind of asymptotic giant branch star L<SUB>2</SUB> Pup
question: What is the morpho-kinematics of the wind escaping the gravity of the AGB star L2 Pup, including line broadening in the nascent wind near the star and the presence of predicted collimated radial outflows?

data.angular_resolution: Typically 20 mas (1.3 au) for first set; 340 mas (22 au) for second set
data.sensitivity: Noise (1 sigma): 2.4 mJy beam^-1 (12CO 3-2), 2.2 mJy beam^-1 (13CO 3-2), 1.5 mJy beam^-1 (29SiO 8-7), 10 mJy beam^-1 (28SiO 5-4), 2.5 mJy beam^-1 (12CO 2-1)

what.value: Hipparcos distance to L2 Pup of 64+-4 pc

evidence.quote: Hipparcos locates it at 64$\pm$4 pc (cite: vanLeeuwen2007).

what.value: Stellar mass of L2 Pup measured as 0.66+-0.05 M_odot

evidence.quote: it is now measured as 0.66$\pm$0.05 M$_\odot$ by (cite: Kervella2016) from the Keplerian motion of the gas orbiting it.

what.value: Systemic LSR velocity V_lsr = 33.3 km s^-1

evidence.quote: Doppler velocities $V_z$ are referred to the same radial velocity relative to the Local Standard of Rest as used by (cite: Homan2017), $V_{lsr}$=33.3 km s$^{-1}$.

what.value: Absorption spectrum of R Dor measured inside a circle of 35 mas radius

evidence.quote: we show in the left panel of Figure 5 the case of R Dor, the other nearby such star, measured inside a circle of 35 mas radius (cite: Nhung2021).

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image high-resolution Band 7 lines (12CO(3-2), 13CO(3-2), 29SiO(8-7)) and medium-resolution Band 6 lines (12CO(2-1), 28SiO(5-4))
recipe.method: Calibrate first set following Kervella et al. (2016) and Homan et al. (2017) and clean in CASA with natural weighting and no continuum subtraction; calibrate second set using standard ALMA scripts without continuum subtraction, shift phase centres to continuum peaks, merge C36-2 and C36-5 configurations, and clean in GILDAS with natural weighting.
key_parameters: Natural weighting, no continuum subtraction, V_lsr = 33.3 km s^-1

recipe.goal: Measure absorption over the stellar disc and radial extent of self-absorption
recipe.method: Extract spectra inside a circle of 12 mas radius centred on L2 Pup for 12,13CO(3-2) and 29SiO(8-7), compare with R Dor, and construct PV maps of V_z vs R in four quadrants (northern, eastern, southern, western).
assumptions: Inner rim of gas disc is at R ~ 31 mas so r < 12 mas receives no contribution from rotation

recipe.goal: Evaluate high Doppler velocity wings, line broadening near the star, and inner disc rotation velocities
recipe.method: Scan line profiles along x = 0 in steps of y = 10 mas (0.64 au) and evaluate the velocity V_{z,20} at which 20% of the maximal flux density is reached on the blue side; compute mean Doppler velocity averaged over R in successive rings (30-60, 60-90, 90-120, 120-150 mas) and integrated over |V_z| < 20 km s^-1 as a function of position angle.
key_parameters: Scan step y = 10 mas (0.64 au) along x = 0; V_{z,20} at 20% of max flux density on blue side; ring intervals 30-60, 60-90, 90-120, 120-150 mas; |V_z| < 20 km s^-1
assumptions: Gaussian line profile approximation to convert V_{z,20} to effective FWHM line width

recipe.goal: Parameterize large-scale wind morpho-kinematics within 200 au using 12CO(2-1) and 28SiO(5-4)
recipe.method: Construct intensity maps, radial distributions, moment 1 maps, and PV maps (V_z vs R and V_z vs omega) for 12CO(2-1) and 28SiO(5-4). In 0.5 arcsec radial intervals from R = 1 to 3.5 arcsec, model V_z vs omega flux density as the sum of three Gaussian-smeared sine waves (amplitudes a, b, c) and derive the inclination and expansion velocity of a flared expanding disc.
key_parameters: Sine wave 1 (dominant, coeff b): V_z = 1.64 sin(omega - 57 deg); Sine wave 2 (coeff a): 1.50 sin(omega - 230 deg); Sine wave 3 (coeff c): 2.43 sin(omega - 208 deg); Gaussian smearing sigma_Vz = 0.55 km s^-1, sigma_omega = 15 deg; radial intervals of 0.5 arcsec from 1.0 to 3.5 arcsec
assumptions: Flared disc with Gaussian distribution of flaring angles (rms sigma_fl) and constant velocity smearing sigma_Vz = 0.55 km s^-1; V_exp = 1.6 / sin(i) km s^-1

recipe.goal: Estimate the mass loss rate from 12CO(2-1) emission
recipe.method: Measure the 12CO(2-1) brightness at a sphere of 2 arcsec radius, convert to column density using optically thin conversion factors f_T from Table 1, and multiply by the annual area swept by the wind given the sky-projected expansion velocity.
key_parameters: R = 2 arcsec; 12CO(2-1) brightness = 1.0 Jy arcsec^-2 km s^-1; mean sine wave amplitude = 1.7 +- 0.5 km s^-1; inclination i = 40 +- 20 deg
assumptions: Optically thin layer at T = 50 K; distance = 64 pc (1 arcsec = 0.96x10^15 cm); abundance ratio CO/H = 10^-4; terminal velocity reached at R = 2 arcsec

recipe.goal: Search for north-south bipolar outflows and blue-shifted emission features near the star
recipe.method: Integrate 12,13CO(3-2) and 29SiO(8-7) intensity maps over |V_z| < 1 km s^-1 within R < 0.2 arcsec; construct PV map (V_z vs y) of 12CO(2-1) integrated within a north-south wedge |sin(omega)| < 0.5 (+-30 deg from y-axis); map 12CO(2-1) and 28SiO(5-4) integrated between -3 and -5 km s^-1.
key_parameters: |V_z| < 1 km s^-1 for Band 7 lines; |sin(omega)| < 0.5 wedge for CO(2-1); velocity range -5 to -3 km s^-1 for northern blob

answer_key.quantity: Possible expansion velocity of the inner gas and dust disc

evidence.quote: Its slightly negative Doppler shift (also visible on the $^{29}$SiO absorption spectrum of Figure 5) may reveal a possible expansion of the disc, at the level of 0.8$\pm$0.5 km s$^{-1}$.

answer_key.quantity: Radius of inner line broadening region

evidence.quote: In summary, in spite of being qualitative, this analysis has shown reliably that significant line broadening is observed at projected distances from the star below $\sim$4 au and is absent above.

answer_key.quantity: Effective line width (FWHM) of 13CO(3-2) beyond 4 au

evidence.quote: The values obtained for $^{13}$CO (right panel of Figure 8) are less affected by absorption and are $\sim$5 km s$^{-1}$ and $\sim$20 km s$^{-1}$, respectively .

Evidence for the apparent normality of the wind launching mechanism has been obtained from the presence of large velocities within $\sim$4 au from the centre of the star, the line width increasing from $\sim$5 km s$^{-1}$ FWHM beyond this distance to $\sim$20 km s$^{-1}$ near the star.

answer_key.quantity: Effective line width (FWHM) near the surface of the star

evidence.quote: In the approximation of Gaussian line profiles, we estimate that the effective line width (FWHM) remains below 10 km s$^{-1}$down to projected distances of $\sim$4 au and then increases linearly to reach $\sim$20 km s$^{-1}$ near the surface of the star.

answer_key.quantity: Rotation velocity amplitude B in inner ring (30 < R < 60 mas) for 12CO(3-2)
Rotation velocity amplitude B in inner ring (30 < R < 60 mas) for 13CO(3-2)
Rotation velocity amplitude B in inner ring (30 < R < 60 mas) for 29SiO(8-7)

evidence.quote: As commonly observed in oxygen-rich AGB stars, the SiO emission is confined near the star, here within $\sim$80 au, and displays therefore a slightly broader Doppler velocity spectrum

answer_key.quantity: Amplitude of dominant sine wave in 12CO(2-1) V_z vs omega

evidence.quote: What can be stated with confidence is the dominance of a sine wave with amplitude 1.6$\pm$0.1 km s$^{-1}$ and a phase of 54$^\circ$$\pm$6$^\circ$, as obtained from a fit to the right panel of Figure 5, together with a flow of about half the intensity in phase opposition.

answer_key.quantity: Phase of dominant sine wave in 12CO(2-1) V_z vs omega

evidence.quote: What can be stated with confidence is the dominance of a sine wave with amplitude 1.6$\pm$0.1 km s$^{-1}$ and a phase of 54$^\circ$$\pm$6$^\circ$, as obtained from a fit to the right panel of Figure 5, together with a flow of about half the intensity in phase opposition.

answer_key.quantity: Position angle of projection of large-scale expanding disc axis on sky plane

evidence.quote: The position angle of the projection of the disc axis on the plane of the sky is simply 54$^\circ$+90$^\circ$$=$144$^\circ$$\pm$6$^\circ$.

answer_key.quantity: Inclination angle i of large-scale expanding wind disc

evidence.quote: Yet, too thin a disc would be highly improbable in the CSE of an AGB star and we retain as a reasonable range of acceptable values of $i$ the interval [20$^\circ$,60$^\circ$], which we write as 40$^\circ$$\pm$20$^\circ$, it being understood that this estimate rests on sensible but somewhat arbitrary arguments.

answer_key.quantity: Upper limit to radial expansion velocity of large-scale wind disc

evidence.quote: Beyond $\sim$1 arcsec from the centre of the star, the wind of L$_2$ Pup is dominated by a disc, or equatorial enhancement, expanding isotropically with a radial velocity not exceeding some 5 km s$^{-1}$, inclined in the north-west/south-east direction with respect to the sky plane by $\sim$40$^\circ$$\pm$20$^\circ$.

answer_key.quantity: Mass loss rate of L2 Pup

evidence.quote: In one year, the wind covers therefore an area of 2$\upi$$R$$\times$0.006=0.08$\pm$0.05 arcsec$^2$, meaning a mass loss rate of 0.08$\times$1.5$\times$10$^{-7}$=(1.2$\pm$0.7)$\times$10$^{-8}$ M$_\odot$yr$^{-1}$.
The mass loss rate has been evaluated at the level of (1.2$\pm$0.7)$\times$10$^{-8}$ M$_\odot$yr$^{-1}$.

not_stated_but_needed: Software versions for both CASA and GILDAS
Deconvolution stopping criteria (threshold, niter) and masking strategies used in CASA and GILDAS cleaning
Image dimensions (number of pixels) for both Band 6 and Band 7 cubes
Exact details of the self-calibration or calibration procedures inherited from Kervella et al. (2016) and Homan et al. (2017)
Exact density and velocity profile assumed for the isotropic wind model used in the uv-coverage distortion test
missing_for_reproduction: CLEAN thresholds, number of iterations, and masking parameters for both CASA and GILDAS imaging
Exact self-calibration parameters for the Band 7 data (deferred to Kervella et al. 2016 and Homan et al. 2017)
Scripts used for the custom PV-diagram sinusoidal fitting and uv-plane isotropic wind simulation
score_reason: Raw archival data are public with a single clear project code, phase-centre shifts and beam/channel/noise parameters are explicitly tabulated in Table 1, and the analytical formulas for column density, mass loss rate, and sinusoidal PV parameterization are written out in full. However, software versions, cleaning stopping criteria, and scripts for the custom PV fitting are not provided, and Band 7 calibration is deferred to earlier papers.
rediscovery_reason: Public archival ALMA data (2015.1.00141.S) with clear empirical targets (line broadening radius ~4 au, outer wind sine-wave amplitude 1.6+-0.1 km s^-1 and PA 144+-6 deg, and mass loss rate 1.2e-8 M_odot yr^-1) that can be directly extracted from cleaned spectral cubes using standard PV and spectral analysis.
